name: Rizpah (Saul's concubine)
title: The Mourning Mother
summary: Rizpah was Saul's concubine and the mother of two of his sons. She is best known for her touching and steadfast vigil over the bodies of her dead sons after they were executed by the Gibeonites, an act that lasted several months and moved King David to give them a proper burial.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Saul's concubine
keyEvents.description: Rizpah is introduced as Saul's concubine and the mother of two of his sons, Armoni and Mephibosheth.

keyEvents.title: Abner's alleged relationship with Rizpah
keyEvents.description: After Saul's death, Ish-bosheth accused the commander Abner of having slept with Rizpah, which led to a serious conflict and Abner's defection to David.

keyEvents.title: The Sons Handed Over to the Gibeonites
keyEvents.description: Because of Saul's breach of the covenant with the Gibeonites, Rizpah's two sons along with five other descendants of Saul were handed over to be executed.

keyEvents.title: The Long Watch Over the Dead
keyEvents.description: Rizpah kept watch over the bodies from the beginning of the barley harvest until rain fell, protecting them from birds and wild animals—a period lasting several months.

keyEvents.title: David Gives the Dead a Dignified Burial
keyEvents.description: When David heard about Rizpah's faithful guarding, he was moved and ensured that all those executed, as well as the bones of Saul and Jonathan, were buried in the family tomb.
